title: Practical Significance | Episode 45: Statistics in the Community (STATCOM)—Service in Action
text:
This month, Annie Cohen and Hanna Venera join Practical Significance co-hosts Donna LaLonde and Ron Wasserstein to discuss their roles as co-presidents of STATCOM at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor. They can’t contain their enthusiasm for this special initiative and the intrinsic reward of working within the community, although they acknowledge the challenges of maintaining momentum as students graduate and leadership changes hands.
Having benefited from being part of a dynamic program, Cohen and Venera have a long-term vision to reinvigorate STATCOM programs on campuses nationwide and are highly motivated to spread awareness. If you have questions about STATCOM, email statcom-um@umich.edu.
Give it a listen here!

title: Hanna Venera, MS
text:
I am a Biostatistics PhD candidate at the University of Michigan, with an expected graduation date of May 2027. I work with Dr. Kelley Kidwell and Dr. Bingkai Wang on statistical methods for Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trials (SMARTs).
My dissertation develops methods for zero-inflated longitudinal outcomes and baseline-adjusted estimation in SMARTs. My broader interests include adaptive interventions, clinical trials, longitudinal data analysis, and statistical methods for improving the precision and interpretability of treatment comparisons.
I earned an MS in Biostatistics from the University of Michigan in 2023 and a BS in Financial Mathematics and BA in Economics from Pacific Lutheran University in 2021.

Leadership and Service

Statistics in the Community
Since 2021, I have supported community-engaged statistical consulting through Statistics in the Community (STATCOM). My leadership roles have included co-president, treasurer, CTAC liaison, and national presence chair.
I have helped scope and direct consulting projects, mentor student consultants, coordinate relationships with community partners, manage budgets and fundraising, and establish a national chapter network and annual meeting.

title: Research
text: My research focuses on statistical methods for adaptive interventions and Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trials (SMARTs), with particular attention to complex outcomes and efficient treatment comparisons.

title: Research
text:
Baseline-adjusted estimation in SMARTs
I am developing ANCOVA-style estimators that use baseline covariates to improve precision when comparing dynamic treatment regimes in SMARTs. This work evaluates common and regime-specific adjustment strategies and develops calibrated, variance-minimizing estimators designed to prevent efficiency loss under model misspecification.
My work includes theoretical development, simulation studies in R, and applications to trial data.

title: Research
text:
Zero-inflated longitudinal outcomes
I developed marginal and conditional hurdle models for longitudinal count outcomes with excess zeros in SMARTs. These methods use weighted-and-replicated generalized estimating equations and g-computation to estimate treatment-regimen-specific zero probabilities and positive-count means.
I evaluated these methods through simulation studies and applied them to data from the SafERteens M-Coach trial. A manuscript describing this work is currently under review.

title: Research
text:
Collaborative research
My collaborative projects include:

Statistical and programming quality review for SMARTs.
Analysis of the financial burden of oral cancer treatments, including financial assistance, out-of-pocket costs, and treatment initiation.
Evaluation of methods for analyzing multiple outcomes with differing hypotheses in platform trials.
Previous research on SMART designs with survival and time-to-event outcomes.
Mobile-health and adaptive-intervention studies involving SMART and micro-randomized trial data.
